rules.handoff: Ultracite's Oxlint adapter (packages/cli/src/agent-fix/linters.ts runOxlintPass, mirrored in scripts/ultracite-adapters.cjs and checked against the CLI by the self-test), run on the project as `ultracite fix` runs it: oxlint --fix, oxfmt --write, then oxlint -f json; then the handoff filter. The config is the root config `ultracite init --linter oxlint` writes, with the user's one change: rules: { "max-lines-per-function": "error" } (its default, 50).
rules.filter: max-lines-per-function, and any other diagnostic that isn't among the prepared project's own (rule and message, file by file, as diff.ts matches them), in the handoff and in every re-lint: a project that lints clean apart from the length limit. A deviation from a real project, where Ultracite would hand over the subject's other diagnostics too. `verifyRemainingLengthRuleOnly` records what a filter keeping the length rule alone would have handed back. A diagnostic whose message carries a count (complexity's score, the limit's own line count) is a new diagnostic to diff.ts once the count changes.
rules.retryLoop: index.ts attemptFileFix: after each attempt, verify (the Oxlint pass on the file, in place, then the filter) and, while diagnostics remain that the agent didn't list on a `Left for review:` line and it didn't time out, another attempt with buildRetryPrompt, up to MAX_AGENT_ATTEMPTS; each attempt under AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS

views.oxlint user: the user's config: what `ultracite init --linter oxlint` writes (extends [core]) with max-lines-per-function on; the handoff's view
views.oxlint strict: the same with max-lines, max-params and max-statements also on at their defaults: what a stricter user would see
views.oxlint sonarjs: Oxlint with SonarJS's cognitive complexity at 20 through jsPlugins, as the js-plugins preset runs it, alone
views.eslint length: what `ultracite init --linter eslint` writes (core), with max-lines-per-function, max-lines, max-params, max-statements, sonarjs/max-lines-per-function and sonarjs/max-lines on at their defaults (core already has sonarjs/cognitive-complexity at 20 and complexity at 20)
views.biome length: what `ultracite init --linter biome` writes (core), with noExcessiveLinesPerFunction, useMaxParams, noExcessiveStatementsPerFunction (nursery) and noExcessiveLinesPerFile on at their defaults (core already has noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity), `biome check`
views.modes: honor = inline config honoured; ignore = every eslint-/oxlint-disable, biome-ignore and @ts-* directive neutralised (ESLint: noInlineConfig)

rules.states: each attempt is measured as the agent left the file (agent), as Oxfmt alone would leave it (agent.formatted), and as verify's fix pass and formatter left it (verified), which is what the next attempt gets and what stays in the project
rules.oracle: research/corpus/scripts/length-oracle.cjs, unchanged: A 400 configs through clientInjectionsPlugin's buildStart and transform; B 300 tag lists through executeRevalidates and withExecuteRevalidates, every call recorded; C 1,938 texts × settings through guessIndentation. The verdict is against the prepared subject; `ignoringKeyOrder` sorts every object's keys first (normalising sorted A's define object). Its `structure` measure gives the functions and entry lines afterwards and each helper's parameters, lines and call sites, and whether the helpers appear in the order the entry calls them

edits.table or loop rewrite: five or more `.replace` calls gone, or a new `.reduce`, with no new named function

This rule checks the number of lines in a function body and reports a diagnostic if it exceeds a specified limit. Remember that this rule only counts the lines of code in the function body, not the entire function declaration.
Some people consider large functions a code smell. Large functions tend to do a lot of things and can make it hard following what’s going on. Many coding style guides dictate a limit of the number of lines that a function can comprise of. This rule can help enforce that style.

- **New helper `createHmrReplacements`** (`clientInjections.ts:223`, 44 lines): this is the old WebSocket/HMR logic, moved unchanged. - **`createClientConfigValueReplacer`** (`clientInjections.ts:268`, now 41 lines, down from 72): it still resolves the hostname, port and server host. It calls the helper and builds the mode, base, server host, WebSocket token and forward-console replacements itself.

The new object's keys are in alphabetical order, matching the rest of the file. A few values are now escaped in a different order than before, which has no visible effect: escaping only runs `JSON.stringify`, which is pure for these strings, numbers, booleans and nulls, and the forward-console value is still escaped after all the others.

I fixed both issues in `clientInjections.ts`. I couldn't re-run the linter or type checker because the folder has no `node_modules`, so I checked the complexity count by hand.

**1. Complexity of `createHmrReplacements` (line 223).** Most of the score came from nine `wsConfig?.` optional-chaining reads, and the rule counts each one as a branch. `wsConfig` now falls back to an empty object `{}` when no ws config is set, with an explicit type, so plain property reads work. Reading a field from `{}` gives `undefined`, the same result `?.` gave on `undefined`, so behaviour doesn't change. By my count, complexity drops from 25 to 16, under the limit of 20. The rest of the previous edit's split is unchanged.

**2. func-style on line 268.** `createClientConfigValueReplacer` is now a `const` holding an `async` arrow function, with the same parameters, return type and body. It's only called inside `buildStart`, which runs after the module has loaded, so declaring it with `const` after the plugin function doesn't break anything at runtime.

path.finalMessage:
I fixed both issues in `clientInjections.ts`. I couldn't run the linter or type-checker here (the shell command needed approval), so this is checked by hand only.

**1. complexity (line 223):** `resolveHmrClientValues` had nine optional-chain reads on `wsConfig` (`wsConfig?.host`, `wsConfig?.port` and so on), and each one adds to the complexity score. `wsConfig` now falls back to an empty object `{}` instead of `undefined`. Every field on it is optional, so reading a missing one still gives `undefined`, the same as `wsConfig?.x` did. That means the `?.` could become plain `.` and behavior stays the same. By my count, complexity drops from 25 to 16, under the limit of 20. The variable has an explicit type, `Exclude<ResolvedConfig["server"]["ws"], false | undefined>`, so TypeScript accepts the `{}` fallback.

**2. func-style (line 265):** `createClientConfigValueReplacer` is now an `async` arrow function assigned to a `const`. Moving off a hoisted declaration is safe: the only caller is the plugin's `buildStart` hook, which runs after the module has loaded.

I also converted `resolveHmrClientValues` to a `const` arrow function. It's a new function declaration at line 223, so func-style should flag it too. My guess is that the report showed only one issue per line and listed complexity there, but I can't confirm that without running the linter. I left `escapeReplacement` as it is because it wasn't flagged.

preserveBehaviour: That means the `?.` could become plain `.` and behavior stays the same.

It came from the previous edit and breaks the same rule, and adding the helper above it would probably have made the linter report it at its new line. I left the older function declarations above line 223, including `escapeReplacement`, as they were.

Runtime behavior should be unchanged. All the new `const` functions are defined before anything calls them. `clientInjectionsPlugin` refers to `createClientConfigValueReplacer` earlier in the file, but only inside `buildStart`, which runs after the module has finished loading, so the later definition isn't a problem.

I fixed issue 1 by splitting `revalidateTags` into three helper functions. It is now 44 lines long, under the 50-line limit. I couldn't confirm that with the linter: running `npx oxlint` needed approval, which a non-interactive run can't get. So the line counts here are my own count, and the file hasn't been type-checked either.

The code that moved out:

- **`findExistingProfileKey(tagsByProfile, profile)`** has the inner loop that looks for a profile key already in the map. It now returns as soon as it finds a match instead of setting a variable and breaking out. It uses the same three comparisons in the same order.
- **`groupTagsByProfile(tagsWithProfile)`** builds and returns the map of tags grouped by profile. It keeps the original `existingKey || profile` fallback.
- **`getProfileDurations(profile, workStore)`** turns a profile into its durations. It still throws the same "Invalid profile provided…" error for a profile name that isn't configured.
- **`TagsByProfile`** is a new type for the map, so its long type isn't written out twice.

Behaviour should be unchanged:

- `getCacheHandlers()` is still called before the tags are grouped.
- `getProfileDurations` is still only called when `profile` is truthy, and at the same point in the loop. So an invalid profile still throws after the earlier groups' promises have already been added, as before.
- The comments are kept, and nothing outside `revalidateTags` was touched.

`withExecuteRevalidates` (line 89) calls `executeRevalidates` before it's defined in the file. That's still safe as a `const`, because the call only runs when the function is invoked, after the module has finished loading. The other two converted functions only call helpers defined above them.

The other function declarations in the file weren't in your report, so I left them alone to keep the change minimal. If the re-lint flags them for `func-style` too, they need the same change.

params: Their parameters, return types, `async` and `export` are unchanged.

path.finalMessage:
I split `revalidateTags` into two helpers and the function itself into what's left, which should clear issue 1. I couldn't run oxlint to confirm because the command needed approval that this non-interactive run can't give. Counting by hand, the three functions are now 36, 45 and 37 lines, all under the 50-line limit.

What changed in `revalidation-utils.ts`:

- **`groupTagsByProfile(tagsWithProfile)`** (line 158): the code that groups tags by profile, moved over as it was. It returns the grouped map.
- **`resolveProfileDurations(profile, workStore)`** (line 204): the code that turns a profile into its `durations` value, also moved over as it was. That includes the `Invalid profile provided …` error for unknown string profiles.
- **`revalidateTags`** (line 242): still returns early on empty input and gets the cache handlers first. It then calls the two helpers and pushes the `updateTags` / `revalidateTag` calls as before.
- I added a small `TagProfile` type alias so the profile key type isn't written out in several places.

Behaviour should be unchanged. Everything runs in the same order, comments are kept, and the "invalid profile" error is still thrown inside the async `revalidateTags`. Callers still see a rejected promise, and calls already pushed for earlier profiles aren't awaited, as before.

path.finalMessage:
I fixed both `func-style` errors by turning the two flagged function declarations into `const` arrow functions. I couldn't re-run the linter or the type checker, because the project has no `node_modules` installed.

- **Issue 1 (line 242):** `revalidateTags` is now `const revalidateTags = async (...): Promise<void> => { ... };`.
- **Issue 2 (line 279):** `executeRevalidates` is now `export const executeRevalidates = (...): false | Promise<void> => { ... };`.

Neither function uses `this`, and their parameters, return types and bodies are unchanged. Switching to `const` drops hoisting, but nothing here depends on it:
- `executeRevalidates` calls `revalidateTags`, which is defined above it.
- `withExecuteRevalidates` uses `executeRevalidates` only inside its own body, so the call happens after the module has finished loading.

The other function declarations in the file weren't flagged, so I left them as they are.

path.finalMessage:
I fixed both issues by splitting the two long functions into smaller top-level helpers. I put the helpers at the top level on purpose, because the rule also counts the lines of any function nested inside another. The logic is the same as before; it just lives in different functions.

I counted the new function lengths by hand but couldn't re-run the linter: oxlint isn't installed here, and the `tsc` type-check needed approval, which I can't get in this run.

**1. `spacesDiff`: 88 → 49 lines**
- `commonPrefixLength` finds where the two indentation strings start to differ.
- `countSpacesAndTabs` replaces the two near-identical counting loops for `a` and `b`.
- `looksLikeAlignment` holds the nested alignment check and returns `true` only in the case that used to set the flag. `spacesDiff` resets the flag to `false` at the start, so the result is the same.

**2. `guessIndentation`: 134 → 33 lines**
- `scanLineIndentation` reads one line's text and indentation. It calls `getLineLength`, `getLineContent` and `getLineCharCode` in the same order as before.
- `collectIndentationStats` runs the main loop (47 lines). It still uses a single `SpacesDiffResult` for every line and still caps at 10k lines.
  - `countIndentedLine` adds to the tab-indented and space-indented line counts.
  - `scoreSpacesDiff` does the alignment skip check (with its original comment) and adds to the `tabSize` scores. It returns `false` when the loop should `continue`, so the previous-line values are still not updated for skipped lines.
- `guessTabSize` picks the best-scoring tab size and keeps the rule that 2 beats 4 when it has at least 2/3 as many occurrences.
- `ALLOWED_TAB_SIZE_GUESSES` and `MAX_ALLOWED_TAB_SIZE_GUESS` are now constants at the top of the file, so they stay next to each other even though different helpers use them.

One small runtime difference: `countSpacesAndTabs` creates a small object on each call, so the main loop now allocates a few short-lived objects per line, where the old code allocated none.

path.finalMessage:
I fixed all 15 issues in `indentationGuesser.ts`. I couldn't re-run the linter because oxlint isn't installed anywhere I could reach, so I checked each fix by hand.

- **Inline comments (1–5):** The comments on the three `IIndentationStats` fields and the two `previousLine…` variables now sit on their own lines above the code. The text is unchanged.
- **Shadowing (6):** I renamed the module-level function `spacesDiff` to `computeSpacesDiff` and updated its one call site in `collectIndentationStats`. Inside it, `const spacesDiff` no longer hides an outer name. This also clears a second, unlisted shadow: `looksLikeAlignment` has a parameter called `spacesDiff`. The function isn't exported, so nothing outside the file is affected.
- **func-style (7, 8, 10–15):** Every function declaration is now an arrow function assigned to a `const`, and `guessIndentation` becomes `export const guessIndentation = (...) => {...}`. I also converted `commonPrefixLength` and `countSpacesAndTabs`, which the rule covers but which weren't in your list, so the whole file uses one style. None of these functions uses `this`, and each is defined before anything calls it, so moving away from hoisted declarations doesn't change behaviour.
- **Function length (9):** In `computeSpacesDiff`, the two 5-line `countSpacesAndTabs(...)` calls are now one-line calls into `aCounts`/`bCounts`, followed by the same destructuring. That brings the function from 55 lines to 49, under the limit of 50. Moving the comments made `collectIndentationStats` 49 lines too.

hand.helpers: Nine helpers. spacesDiff became computeSpacesDiff (5 parameters, mutates its result) with commonPrefixLength, countSpacesAndTabs and looksLikeAlignment; the guess loop stays in collectIndentationStats with scoreSpacesDiff (4 parameters; adds to the scores and returns whether to skip the line) and countIndentedLine (mutates the counts); scanLineIndentation and guessTabSize; constants moved to module scope. Entry 33 lines.
quotes: It returns `false` when the loop should `continue`, so the previous-line values are still not updated for skipped lines.
I put the helpers at the top level on purpose, because the rule also counts the lines of any function nested inside another.
hand.notes: Mild gaming in attempt 2: it rewrote two wrapped countSpacesAndTabs calls as one-line calls into intermediate variables to take computeSpacesDiff from 55 lines to 49. Ultracite had handed the 55-line report back as new, under 'The previous edit resolved the issues it was given'.
hand.readerReason: The loop keeps its continues and previous-line updates, but scoring is a helper that both mutates the stats and returns whether to skip, and counting the indented line is a two-branch helper of its own; nine helpers in all.
hand.reader2Reason: The spacesDiff helpers, scanLineIndentation and guessTabSize are clean seams, and the previous-line state stays local. But countIndentedLine is a trivial mutating helper, and scoreSpacesDiff both mutates stats and returns a boolean that drives the caller's continue, so the loop body is somewhat fragmented.

I split both long functions into helpers in `indentationGuesser.ts`. Behaviour should be unchanged. I couldn't run oxlint, tsc or any tests here because those commands needed approval in this non-interactive session. So I checked the function lengths by reading the file, and the line ranges below are my own count.

**1. `spacesDiff` (was 88 lines, now about 43)** — I moved three pieces out into helpers:
- `commonPrefixLength()` finds how long the shared indentation is.
- `countSpacesAndTabs()` replaces the two copied counting loops. It returns a `[spaces, tabs]` pair, so each call fits on one line.
- `looksLikeAlignment()` holds the nested alignment check and its comment. `spacesDiff` still checks `spacesDiff > 0` first, as before.

**2. `guessIndentation` (was 134 lines, now about 33)** — it now just calls the helpers and decides tabs or spaces:
- `readLineIndentation()` reads one line's indentation. It calls the text buffer in the same order as before: line length, then content, then individual character codes.
- `collectIndentationStats()` loops over the first 10k lines, skips blank ones and counts tab-indented and space-indented lines.
- `scoreLine()` compares each line with the previous one and records the result. Each `continue` in the old loop is now a `return`, so skipped alignment lines still don't count and don't become the "previous line".
- `guessTabSize()` picks the best tab size and keeps the rule that lets 2 beat 4.
- I moved `ALLOWED_TAB_SIZE_GUESSES` and `MAX_ALLOWED_TAB_SIZE_GUESS` to the top level of the file. Neither is ever modified, so this changes nothing.

All new functions are under 50 lines, the longest being `readLineIndentation` at about 40. I added no suppression comments and touched no other file.

hand.readerReason: The loop body moved into a five-parameter helper that mutates a statistics object and returns early to skip alignment lines, so the skip and the previous-line update are no longer visible in the loop; line data is typed as ReturnType<typeof ...>.
hand.reader2Reason: The spacesDiff helpers and guessTabSize help. But the per-line loop is split between collectIndentationStatistics and updateIndentationStatistics, a five-parameter function that mutates a shared statistics object and early-returns to skip lines, with its line type coupled via ReturnType<typeof getLineIndentation>. That offsets the gains.

hand.helpers: Five helpers; updateIndentationStats (4 parameters) holds the whole loop body, mutates the stats object and returns early on alignment lines; setSpacesDiffWithAlignment (5 parameters) writes into the result; readLineIndentation, guessTabSize, countIndentation. Entry 42 lines.
quotes: The alignment checks have a subtle effect: skipped lines still affect the tabs-versus-spaces count, but don’t become the previous line for comparison.
hand.notes: The c06 shape, behaviour kept.
hand.readerReason: The whole loop body is in updateIndentationStats, which mutates a stats object and returns early on alignment lines, so the entry's loop no longer shows what is counted or skipped.
hand.reader2Reason: countIndentation, readLineIndentation and guessTabSize help. But setSpacesDiffWithAlignment mutates the result out-parameter under a name that hides what it sets, and updateIndentationStats mutates a shared stats object (including tmp and the previous-line state) for the whole per-line step, so the scoring is harder to trace.
